WV10-P01.5.note: Calling a snapped string a 'monster', offering to frame it and bowing are teasing, so Abel is amused; the school-desk detail is background and his reply does not look back on the past (C), nor is it grateful, worried or indignant.

WV10-P03.5.note: Handing back the third letter unsigned and telling him to read before writing 'a fourth' shows impatience, so irritated fits best; but 'before he wrote a fourth' can be read as dry teasing, so playful (B) can also be defended, and no line in the passage rules it out cleanly.
